rows.bloom_title: The Book of the City of Ladies
rows.title: The Boke Of The Cyte Of Ladyes
rows.translator: Brian Anslay (not named in what I read; standard attribution)
rows.year: 1521 (colophon quoted in IA metadata: 'Imprynted at London... by Henry Pepwell... M.CCCCC.xxj')
rows.djvu: the boke of the cyte of ladyes_djvu.txt
rows.evidence: IA metadata/description read; EEBO facsimile, tesseract 'enm' OCR. Note the djvu file name has spaces.
rows.case: Bloom lists the City of Ladies; the only pre-1931 English is the 1521 Pepwell printing, which is PD.
rows.note: Black-letter EEBO scan: OCR will be rough; a clean transcript exists at quod.lib.umich.edu/e/eebo/A20897.0001.001 (EEBO-TCP, check its terms before using). The modern Richards translation (1982) is copyrighted.

rows.title: The Castell of love
rows.translator: John Bourchier, Lord Berners (read on title page: 'translated oute of Spanyshe into Englyshe by John Bowrchier knyght, lorde Bernes')
rows.year: 1560 (IA metadata; title-page OCR too garbled to read a date)
rows.evidence: Read first 1200 chars of djvu: Berners translator line legible.
rows.case: Bloom lists Cárcel de amor; Berners's Castell of Love is the classic (and only pre-1931) English version.
rows.note: The OCR is black-letter garble; usable only with re-OCR or as a page-image edition. The 1979 Whinnom edition is copyrighted (lending only).

rows.title: The Poems of William Dunbar, ed. John Small, vol. I (Scottish Text Society)
rows.year: 1893 (IA metadata; title page read, date not in the first page)
rows.evidence: Read title: 'The Poems of William Dunbar edited by the late John Small ... Vol. I, introduction by AE. J. G. Mackay'. Volumes 2-3 also on IA (e.g. poemsofwilliamdu03dunbuoft).
rows.case: Bloom lists Dunbar's poems; the Scottish Text Society edition (Small/Mackay) is the standard complete scholarly text.
rows.note: Machine's 'author' hit was Paul Laurence Dunbar - nothing of William Dunbar is held. STS edition is 3 vols; vol. 1 is introduction + poems.

rows.title: The Poetical Works of John Skelton, Volume 1 (of 2)
rows.year: 1843 (preface dated 'London, Gray's Inn, Nov. 1st, 1843' in PG text)
rows.case: Dyce's 1843 Poetical Works is the classic complete Skelton.
rows.note: Held 'skelton' shelf is Philip Skelton (an 18th-c. divine), not John.

rows.title: The Poetical Works of John Skelton, Volume 2 (of 2)
rows.case: Dyce's 1843 Poetical Works is the classic complete Skelton.
rows.note: Held 'skelton' shelf is Philip Skelton (an 18th-c. divine), not John.

rows.title: The Poems of Sir Thomas Wiat, edited from the MSS. and early editions by A. K. Foxwell, vol. I
rows.year: 1913 (title page: '...University of London Press... Hodder and Stoughton ... 1913', OCR ragged)
rows.case: Bloom lists Wyatt's poems; Foxwell (2 vols, 1913) is the first edition from the manuscripts, the Aldine is a handy one-volume text.
rows.note: Vol. II of Foxwell: poemsofsirthomas02wyatuoft.

rows.title: The Poems of Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, ed. Frederick Morgan Padelford
rows.year: 1920 (title page: 'University of Washington Publications ... Volume 1, October, 1920')
rows.case: Padelford's 1920 edition is the modern scholarly Surrey and is PD.
rows.note: IA also has a 1928 revised Padelford (poemsofhenryhowa1928surr) - also pre-1931 - and the Aldine Surrey (1866/1871).

rows.title: The Countess of Pembroke's Arcadia
rows.year: 1907 (PG header: 'Original publication: George Routledge and Sons, 1907'; editor Ernest A. Baker)
rows.case: Bloom lists the Arcadia; PG 70854 is Baker's edition of the composite Arcadia.
rows.note: Nothing of Sir Philip Sidney is held (machine matched other Sidneys).

rows.title: Sir P.S.: His Astrophel and Stella
rows.year: 1591 (PG text reproduces title: 'At London, Printed for Thomas Newman. Anno Domini 1591')
rows.case: PG 56375 is a transcription of the first (Newman 1591) quarto.
rows.note: Old spelling. PG 1962 (Defence of Poesie and Poems) also contains the sonnets in a modernized text.

rows.title: A Defence of Poesie and Poems
rows.year: 1891 (PG credits: 'Transcribed from the 1891 Cassell & Company edition')
rows.case: The Apology for Poetry = The Defence of Poesie; PG 1962 is Henry Morley's Cassell's National Library edition.

rows.title: The Works in Verse and Prose Complete of Fulke Greville, Lord Brooke, ed. Grosart, vol. III (Caelica; Alaham; Mustapha)
rows.year: 1870 (title page: 'Printed for private circulation. 1870. 156 copies only')
rows.case: Bloom lists the poems; Grosart's Works (4 vols) is the only complete edition, Crow's Caelica a clean reading text.
rows.note: Other Grosart vols (02, 04) on IA as worksforfirsttim02broouoft etc.

rows.title: Spenser's Minor Poems, ed. Ernest de Selincourt
rows.year: 1910 (title page: 'Oxford at the Clarendon Press MCMX')
rows.evidence: Read title page and introduction opening.
rows.case: Bloom's title matches de Selincourt's Oxford volume exactly; we hold only the Faerie Queene.
rows.note: PG 10602 (Child vol. 5) is apparatus only, not the minor poems.

rows.title: The Poems of Sir Walter Ralegh, ed. Agnes M. C. Latham
rows.year: 1929 (title page: 'Houghton Mifflin Company 1929'; printed in Great Britain by MacLehose)
rows.evidence: Read dust-jacket + imprint lines; collection bplhoughton/bostonpubliclibrary (not lending).
rows.case: Latham's 1929 edition is the definitive collection and is PD (1929); Hannah is the older Aldine alternative.

rows.title: The Works of Christopher Marlowe, ed. C. F. Tucker Brooke
rows.year: 1910 first edition; this scan is the 'Impression of 1925' (title verso: 'First edition, 1910 / Impression of 1925')
rows.evidence: Read title page and verso; an unrevised reprint, fine.
rows.case: One-volume complete Marlowe (plays, poems, translations); we hold only Doctor Faustus (and Edward II on mason-poetry).
rows.note: PG has Bullen's Works vols 2-3 (42724, 21262) and single plays if a PG text is preferred.

rows.title: Minor Poems of Michael Drayton, chosen and edited by Cyril Brett
rows.case: Brett's Oxford selection is the best PD reading text of Drayton's lyrics (Idea, odes, Nymphidia).
rows.note: Not complete: Poly-Olbion is excluded. Hebel's complete Works (1931-41) is not PD.

rows.title: Poems and A Defence of Ryme, ed. Arthur Colby Sprague
rows.evidence: Read title page and copyright line; Wellesley copy, collection americana (not lending).
rows.case: Sprague's edition carries exactly Bloom's two Daniel titles; 1930 is PD as of 2026.
rows.note: Grosart's Complete Works (1885, 5 vols) is the full alternative.

rows.title: The Vnfortunate Traveller, or The Life of Jack Wilton, with an essay ... by Edmund Gosse
rows.year: unread (PG text shows 'London, printed and issued by Charles Whittingham & Co at the Chiswick Press'; Gosse's edition is 1892, not read)
rows.case: Bloom lists the Unfortunate Traveller; PG 21338 is the Gosse/Chiswick edition.

rows.title: The Spanish Tragedie
rows.evidence: PG header read; Manly's Specimens text.
rows.case: Both are PD; Manly's is the edited text.

rows.title: Works of Thomas Campion: Songs and Masques, with Observations in the Art of English Poesy, ed. A. H. Bullen
rows.case: Bullen's 1903 Songs and Masques is the classic Campion edition.
rows.note: Avoid workscamp00campuoft: it is a 1966/67 lithographic reprint (unrevised, but prefer a period printing).

rows.title: The Works of Ben Jonson, with a biographical memoir by William Gifford, a new edition
rows.evidence: Read title page; one-volume complete Works (plays, masques, poems).
rows.case: Bloom asks for the poems, plays and masques together; Gifford's one-volume Routledge Works is the handiest complete text.
rows.note: PG has many single plays (Volpone 4039, Alchemist 4081, etc.) and Discoveries+Poems (5134). Gifford/Cunningham 9-vol (1875) also on IA.

rows.title: The Anatomy of Melancholy
rows.year: unread (PG intro: based on a 19th-c. modernized edition corrected against the 1638 edition)
rows.case: Bloom lists Burton's Anatomy; PG 10800 is a complete, corrected text.
rows.note: The 'burton' shelf is Richard Burton (Arabian Nights); Robert Burton is not held.

rows.title: The Hesperides & Noble Numbers: Vol. 1 and 2
rows.year: 1898 (PG text: '1898'; editor Alfred W. Pollard, Muses' Library)
rows.case: Complete Hesperides and Noble Numbers in Pollard's Muses' Library edition.
rows.note: PG 1211 is only Palgrave's selection.

rows.title: The Poems and Masque of Thomas Carew, ed. Joseph Woodfall Ebsworth
rows.case: Ebsworth's complete Poems and Coelum Britannicum masque.
rows.note: Vincent's Muses' Library (1899, poemscarew00careuoft) is an alternative.

rows.title: Lucasta
rows.year: unread (PG text is W. Carew Hazlitt's edition; preface signed 'Kensington, August 12, 1863')
rows.evidence: PG front matter read: includes Lucasta and the Posthume Poems.
rows.case: Hazlitt's Lucasta (with Posthume Poems) is the complete Lovelace.

rows.title: Miscellaneous Poems by Andrew Marvell, Esq.
rows.evidence: Read title page; Nonesuch reprint of the 1681 folio.
rows.case: A faithful reprint of the 1681 Miscellaneous Poems.
rows.note: Avoid poemslettersofan0001edit: it is Margoliouth's corrected 2nd edition (1952), not the 1927 first. PG 26288 is one poem only.

rows.title: The Works of the Right Honourable John, Earl of Rochester
rows.year: 1718 (PG text: 'Printed for the Booksellers of London and Westminster. 1718')
rows.case: An 18th-c. collected Rochester; the only PD collected text on PG.
rows.note: Contains some misattributions typical of early editions.

rows.title: The Complete Works of Richard Crashaw, Volume I
rows.case: Grosart's Complete Works of Crashaw.

rows.title: The Complete Works of Richard Crashaw, Volume II
rows.case: Grosart's Complete Works of Crashaw.

rows.title: The Works of Francis Beaumont and John Fletcher, vol. I, text ed. Arnold Glover (Cambridge English Classics)
rows.evidence: Read title page; vol. I holds Maid's Tragedy, Philaster, A King and No King, Scornful Lady, Custom of the Country.
rows.case: Glover & Waller's 10-vol Cambridge text is the standard complete B&F.
rows.note: PG has the same edition play by play (e.g. 10620, 12039). The held 'john-fletcher' shelf is John Fletcher of Madeley, the Methodist.

rows.title: The Works of George Chapman: Plays, ed. Richard Herne Shepherd, a new edition
rows.evidence: Read title page and start of contents.
rows.case: Shepherd's Chatto edition covers plays and poems.
rows.note: Third vol. is Homer (already partly on PG). PG 20890 has Bussy D'Ambois.

rows.title: The Works of George Chapman: Poems and Minor Translations, intro. Swinburne
rows.case: Shepherd's Chatto edition covers plays and poems.
rows.note: Third vol. is Homer (already partly on PG). PG 20890 has Bussy D'Ambois.

rows.title: John Ford, ed. Havelock Ellis (Mermaid Series)
rows.evidence: Read series title page; grep of djvu shows the 'TIS PITY SHE'S A WHORE running heads.
rows.case: The Mermaid Ford includes 'Tis Pity, The Broken Heart and others.
rows.note: IA also has 'Tis pity she's a whore, and The broken heart (Sherman, 1915).

rows.title: The Works of John Marston. Volume 1
rows.case: Bullen's Works vol. 1 contains The Malcontent.

rows.title: Webster & Tourneur (Mermaid Series)
rows.evidence: PG contents read: The White Devil, The Duchess of Malfi, The Revenger's Tragedy (plus Appius and Virginia).
rows.case: One Mermaid volume covers 188, 189 and 191.
rows.note: Nothing of John Webster is held (machine matched other Websters).

rows.title: The works of Thomas Middleton, Volume 4 (of 5)
rows.year: 1840 (PG header: 'Original publication: Edward Lumley, 1840'; editor Dyce)
rows.evidence: PG text: 'THE CHANGELING.' found in vol. 4.
rows.case: Dyce's Middleton vol. 4 contains The Changeling.

rows.bloom_title: A New Way to Pay Old Debts
rows.title: A New Way to Pay Old Debts
rows.translator: unread (editor not read; likely K. Deighton)
rows.evidence: Grep of djvu: 'MASSINGER'S ... LONDON 1893' and life of Massinger.
rows.case: A school edition of the play; PD.
rows.note: PG 48440 (Massinger vol. I, 1830) does not contain this play. The Mermaid Massinger vol. 1 (Symons) also has it, not checked.

rows.title: The Compleat Angler
rows.evidence: PG catalogue; also PG 9198 (the 1653 first-edition text).
rows.case: Bloom lists Walton's Angler; only Lang's introduction to it is held, not the text.
rows.note: PG 9198 reproduces the 1653 text; 683 is the fuller later text with Cotton's part (not verified which).

rows.title: Brief Lives, Vol. 1
rows.case: Clark's Clarendon edition (1898) is the standard full text.

rows.title: Brief Lives, Vol. 2
rows.case: Clark's Clarendon edition (1898) is the standard full text.

rows.title: Hudibras, in Three Parts
rows.year: 1805 (PG note: 'The text is that of an edition published in London, 1805')
rows.case: Bloom lists Hudibras; the held 'samuel-butler' shelf is the Victorian Samuel Butler (Erewhon), not this one.

rows.title: The Poetical Works of John Dryden, Volume 1 (Gilfillan)
rows.case: We hold Scott's Works vols 11-17 but none of the original poems or plays; the simplest completion is to add Scott vols 2-10 from PG (12166, 37645, 15349, 16208, 16456, 16402, 47679, 49221, 51652) which hold the plays and poems, or Gilfillan's Poetical Works for the poems alone.
rows.note: Recommend completing the Scott set we already started (same edition = consistent citation); vol 1 (Life) and 18 also on PG/IA.

rows.title: The Poetical Works of John Dryden, Volume 2 (Gilfillan)
rows.case: We hold Scott's Works vols 11-17 but none of the original poems or plays; the simplest completion is to add Scott vols 2-10 from PG (12166, 37645, 15349, 16208, 16456, 16402, 47679, 49221, 51652) which hold the plays and poems, or Gilfillan's Poetical Works for the poems alone.
rows.note: Recommend completing the Scott set we already started (same edition = consistent citation); vol 1 (Life) and 18 also on PG/IA.

rows.title: Essays of John Dryden, selected and edited by W. P. Ker, vol. I
rows.evidence: Read title page and preface (Digital Library of India scan, not lending).
rows.case: Ker's 2-vol Essays is the standard collection of Dryden's criticism.
rows.note: PG 2615 (Discourses on Satire and Epic Poetry) is a partial alternative.

rows.title: Essays of John Dryden, vol. 2, ed. W. P. Ker
rows.case: Ker's 2-vol Essays is the standard collection of Dryden's criticism.
rows.note: PG 2615 (Discourses on Satire and Epic Poetry) is a partial alternative.

rows.title: Thomas Otway (Mermaid Series), ed. Roden Noel
rows.case: Mermaid Otway contains Venice Preserv'd and The Orphan.

rows.title: The Way of the World
rows.case: Standard PG text.
rows.note: Held 'congreve' shelf is Richard Congreve (positivist), not William.

rows.title: Love for Love: A Comedy
rows.case: Standard PG text.

rows.title: A Tale of a Tub (ed. Henry Morley)
rows.case: Bloom lists the Tale; PG 4737 is Morley's Cassell text.

rows.title: The Poems of Jonathan Swift, D.D., Volume 1 (ed. W. E. Browning)
rows.case: Browning's Bohn edition is the complete PD Swift poems.

rows.title: The Poems of Jonathan Swift, D.D., Volume 2
rows.case: Browning's Bohn edition is the complete PD Swift poems.

rows.title: The Works of Sir George Etheredge: Plays and Poems, ed. A. Wilson Verity
rows.case: Verity's Works contains The Man of Mode and the other two comedies.

rows.title: The Poetical Works of Alexander Pope, Volume 1 (Gilfillan)
rows.case: We hold two slim Pope selections; Gilfillan's 2-vol Poetical Works gives the whole poetry (Dunciad, Epistles, Windsor Forest, etc.).
rows.note: Elwin-Courthope Works (PG 32190, 43271) is the scholarly alternative but incomplete on PG.

rows.title: The Poetical Works of Alexander Pope, Volume 2 (Gilfillan)
rows.case: We hold two slim Pope selections; Gilfillan's 2-vol Poetical Works gives the whole poetry (Dunciad, Epistles, Windsor Forest, etc.).
rows.note: Elwin-Courthope Works (PG 32190, 43271) is the scholarly alternative but incomplete on PG.

rows.title: The Beggar's Opera
rows.case: Standard PG text.

rows.title: Private Papers of James Boswell from Malahide Castle, in the collection of Lt-Colonel Ralph Heyward Isham (vol. I: 1754-1763)
rows.year: 1928 (title page: 'Copyright, 1928, Ralph H. Isham ... Printed in the United States of America')
rows.evidence: Read title page, note and contents: 'Journal of my Jaunt, Harvest 1762', 'First memoranda of Johnson 1763'; collection internetarchivebooks, djvu downloads.
rows.case: Bloom's 'Journals' are the private journals, first printed in Isham's limited Private Papers (1928-34); the 1928-1930 volumes are US-PD and vol. I is on IA. The Hebrides journal (1785) is the published journal.
rows.note: Only vol. I of Isham was found readable; later vols are lending-only or post-1930 (a 1931 vol. is lending). The Yale trade editions (1950-) are not PD. Notable find.

rows.title: Dr. Johnson's Works: Life, Poems, and Tales, Volume 1 (Works in Nine Volumes)
rows.year: unread (PG header: 'In nine volumes. Volume the first'; the Oxford 1825 edition, not read)
rows.case: Bloom's 'Works': the 9-vol Oxford set is on PG in part; it holds the poems, Rambler, Idler, Adventurer and Lives.
rows.note: PG lacks vols 6, 7, 9 of this set; IA has full Oxford 1825 sets. Lives of the Poets also separately on PG (4679, 9823).

rows.title: The Works of Samuel Johnson, LL.D. in Nine Volumes, Volume 02 The Rambler, Volume I
rows.case: Bloom's 'Works': the 9-vol Oxford set is on PG in part; it holds the poems, Rambler, Idler, Adventurer and Lives.
rows.note: PG lacks vols 6, 7, 9 of this set; IA has full Oxford 1825 sets. Lives of the Poets also separately on PG (4679, 9823).

rows.bloom_title: A Philosophical Enquiry into...the Sublime and Beautiful
rows.title: The Works of the Right Honourable Edmund Burke, Vol. 01 (of 12)
rows.evidence: PG contents read: 'A Philosophical Inquiry into the Origin of our Ideas of the Sublime and Beautiful'.
rows.case: We hold vol. 3 of this same Works; vol. 1 contains the Enquiry - same edition, consistent.

rows.bloom_title: An Essay on the Dramatic Character of Sir John Falstaff
rows.title: Morgann's Essay on the Dramatic Character of Sir John Falstaff, ed. William Arthur Gill
rows.evidence: Read title page and introduction opening.
rows.case: Gill's 1912 reprint is a clean text of the 1777 essay.

rows.title: The Poetical Works of William Collins; With a Memoir
rows.year: unread (PG text shows '1865' in front matter)
rows.case: Complete Collins (a slim oeuvre).

rows.title: The Beaux-Stratagem
rows.case: Standard PG text.

rows.title: The Recruiting Officer (Inchbald's British Theatre)
rows.case: Standard PG text.

rows.title: William Wycherley [Four Plays] (Mermaid Series, ed. W. C. Ward)
rows.year: 1893 (PG front matter: 'Edited, with an introduction and notes ... 1893')
rows.evidence: PG text: 'THE COUNTRY WIFE.' and 'THE PLAIN DEALER.' present.
rows.case: One Mermaid volume covers both Wycherley titles Bloom lists.
rows.note: Mermaid texts are lightly bowdlerised in places? Not checked.

rows.title: A Song to David, by Christopher Smart, edited, with notes
rows.case: A clean annotated reprint of the 1763 poem.
rows.note: IA also has 1904 and 1924 printings.

rows.title: The School for Scandal
rows.case: Standard PG text.
rows.note: Held 'sheridan' hits are Sheridan Le Fanu.

rows.title: The Rivals: A Comedy
rows.case: Standard PG text.

rows.title: The Complete Poetical Works of William Cowper, ed. H. S. Milford (Oxford Edition)
rows.evidence: Read title page and preface; Toronto copy.
rows.case: Milford's Oxford Cowper is the standard complete text; we hold only The Task.
rows.note: PG 47790 (Grimshawe's one-volume Works with letters) is an alternative.

rows.title: George Crabbe: Poems, Volume 1 (of 3) (Cambridge English Classics, ed. A. W. Ward)
rows.case: Ward's 3-vol Cambridge Crabbe is the standard complete text.

rows.title: George Crabbe: Poems, Volume 2 (of 3)
rows.case: Ward's 3-vol Cambridge Crabbe is the standard complete text.

rows.title: George Crabbe: Poems, Volume 3 (of 3)
rows.case: Ward's 3-vol Cambridge Crabbe is the standard complete text.

rows.title: The Expedition of Humphry Clinker
rows.case: Standard PG text.
rows.note: Held smollett-translations shelf holds only his translations (Gil Blas, Don Quixote).

rows.title: The Adventures of Roderick Random
rows.case: Standard PG text.
